preconditions.description: Attacker must be the contract owner to access fee-setting functions
Victim users must hold tokens and attempt to sell/buy on PancakeSwap

violation_target.exploit_hint: 1. Attacker (as owner) calls setSellTaxFeePercent, setSellLiquidityFeePercent, and setSelldevFeePercent to set fees to maximum values (e.g., 100 or higher). 2. Victim users attempt to sell tokens on PancakeSwap. 3. Due to excessive fees, most or all of the victim's tokens are captured as fees instead of being received by the victim. 4. Fees accumulate in the contract and can be extracted by the owner through swapAndLiquify mechanism or direct transfer. 5. Attacker's BNB/token balance increases from the captured fees while victims lose value on their transactions.

attempts.vulnerability_analysis: The xenoX token contract has owner-controlled fee functions (setSellTaxFeePercent, setSellLiquidityFeePercent, setSelldevFeePercent) that allow setting fees up to 100% (calculated as amount.mul(_fee).div(10**2)). The swapAndLiquify mechanism automatically converts accumulated fee tokens to BNB and sends the dev fee portion to _devAddress. An attacker who controls the owner address can set sell fees to 100% dev fee, set _devAddress to themselves, then have victims sell tokens - capturing all the value as BNB fees.
attempts.attack_strategy: 1. Impersonate the contract owner. 2. Set all sell fees to maximize dev fee (100% total). 3. Set _devAddress to attacker's address. 4. Create a victim with tokens. 5. Have victim sell tokens on PancakeSwap (fees accumulate in contract). 6. Contract auto-triggers swapAndLiquify when threshold reached. 7. BNB from dev fees sent to attacker. 8. Verify attacker's BNB balance increased.
attempts.step_by_step_plan: 1. Get owner address from contract. 2. Inject BNB for gas. 3. Impersonate owner to set sell fees (0% tax, 0% liquidity, 100% dev). 4. Set dev address to attacker. 5. Create victim address and inject tokens. 6. Victim approves PancakeSwap router. 7. Victim sells tokens (triggers fee collection). 8. Contract auto-swaps fees to BNB and sends to attacker. 9. Assert attacker BNB balance increased.

attempts.vulnerability_analysis: Looking at the contract more carefully, fees are collected on ANY transfer (not just PancakeSwap). The _transfer function applies fees based on whether from/to is pancakePair. For regular transfers, buy fees apply. I can exploit this by: 1) Setting buy fees to 100% dev fee, 2) Having victim transfer tokens to any address, 3) Fees accumulate in contract, 4) When threshold reached, swapAndLiquify triggers. However, swapAndLiquify needs pair liquidity. Let me check if the mainnet pair already has liquidity, or use a direct transfer approach.
attempts.attack_strategy: Simpler approach: 1. Impersonate owner, set ALL fees (buy and sell) to 100% dev fee. 2. Set dev address to attacker. 3. Have victim transfer tokens directly (not through DEX) - this triggers fee collection. 4. Do multiple transfers to reach the swapAndLiquify threshold. 5. The contract will auto-swap fees to BNB and send to attacker. This avoids complex DEX interactions.
attempts.step_by_step_plan: 1. Impersonate owner, set buy/sell fees to 100% dev fee. 2. Set dev address to attacker. 3. Give victim tokens. 4. Victim transfers tokens to another address (triggers fee collection). 5. Repeat until contract balance reaches threshold (10000 * 1e9). 6. Next transfer triggers swapAndLiquify which sends BNB to attacker. 7. Assert attacker balance increased.
attempts.failure_reflection: The timeout is likely caused by complex PancakeSwap router interactions in the fork environment. The addLiquidityETH and swap operations may be hanging. I need a simpler approach that doesn't rely on DEX operations.
